title: Perfect receiver tracer data did not fix the response to surface renewal loss in an equal-volume two-box model
abstract: Can exact baseline tracer data fix the oxygen response to loss of surface renewal? We test a mass-conserving two-box model with equal known volumes, one surface source, and constant uniform oxygen use. Two positive rate sets have the same full receiver transit-time distribution and initial apparent oxygen utilization (AOU), but differ under the same renewal-rate cut. We prove an exact rate-swap identity and derive the two-branch response set. In a synthetic example with receiver mean age 50 years, a 60% renewal cut gives 36-year AOU gains of 51.43 and 15.28 umol/kg. The factor 3.37 is a synthetic contrast, not a North Pacific uncertainty interval. A source-reservoir mean age identifies the branch. Independent ODE and matrix-exponential solutions agree within 4e-10 umol/kg. This establishes a limit of baseline tracer calibration even with the exact full age distribution. It does not refit the published ocean model or challenge the observed oxygen loss. Spatial observations and independent change tests can remove this ambiguity.

display.caption: Synthetic equal-volume models have identical receiver TTDs and initial AOU, but give different responses to a 60% surface-renewal cut. No observed ocean changes are plotted.

citations.reason: Tests what baseline tracer calibration can identify about renewal response; no ocean-model refit.
Independent oxygen-change validation supplies information beyond baseline calibration.
